newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Bids mostly lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Bids mostly lower.

text.p: Dark northern spring wheat cash prices were mostly weaker on Thursday in line with lower MGE futures, dealers said.

Dealers noted some movement. "I bought about 30,000 bushels, mostly spring wheat, but that was on Wednesday's market, and I bought 10,000 bushels of winter wheat for prompt shipment," a Montana dealer said.
"I think farmers have (more) grain to sell. But they are waiting," the dealer said.
In parts of Minnesota, the Dakotas and Montana, dealers said some grain was moving as a result of milder weather.
A Minneapolis dealer said decent weather in parts of the Northern Plains prompted the movement of grain in Minnesota and the Dakotas.
A few weeks ago, dealers said grain was difficult to move due to harsh winter conditions.

A series of storms after Christmas battered parts of the Midwest and northern tier states. "We managed to keep the trains moving," a Burlington Northern spokesman said. "There have been some delays." But he said the company was getting more locomotives into the system, and grain, coal and merchandise were all moving.
